scene: A round-headed white stick figure with heavy-lidded eyes, an open mouth and sweat drips lies on a wooden bed in a ragged striped linen wrap, one arm dangling toward a blue puddle on the stone floor. At the right stands a large red thermometer whose top is cracked and venting steam, and a window behind shows a crescent moon over two pyramids. Hieroglyph-carved walls and wavy heat squiggles fill the orange room.
mechanism: A single hot-room scene turns the temperature figure in the headline into a visible consequence: the sleeper is drenched and the thermometer is bursting.
composition: The headline spans the top fifth, the sleeper's head and torso make the main focal mass at left-centre, and the tall thermometer is a vertical secondary anchor at far right. The diagonal of the body runs from upper left to the dripping hand, which leads the eye down to the puddle.
typography: Two words in thick-outlined yellow capitals, the degree figure included, fill roughly four fifths of the width and stay fully legible in the 160x90 sheet. The headline adds a specific temperature the title lacks, while the Egyptian setting is carried only by the pyramids and wall carvings.
colors: Orange and terracotta dominate the room, so the saturated red thermometer is the only strong warm-on-warm accent and the yellow headline separates through its black outline. The only cool patch is the dark blue night window, which contrasts with the heat.
psychology: Drooping eyelids, a slack open mouth, sweat drops and a limp hanging arm show visible exhaustion. The cracked, steaming thermometer adds a danger cue for heat.
partnership: The title asks how Egyptians slept without air conditioning, and the thumbnail supplies the hardship through 50°C while leaving the how unanswered. The image does not name Egypt in words, but the pyramids and hieroglyphs align with the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow 50°C headline first, then the sweating sleeper's face, then the red thermometer, then the pyramid window.
art: Flat doodle style with consistent dark outlines and clean fills; the bed, wall tiles and thermometer are coherent in perspective. Background is busy with carvings and squiggles but the saturated headline and figure still survive at phone size.
strength: A concrete number paired with a visibly suffering sleeper makes the premise readable in under a second.
weakness: The busy orange wall pattern competes with the sleeper's thin white figure for attention.
bottleneck: Nothing in the image hints at a method or solution, so the curiosity rests entirely on the number.
action: Hypothesis: test adding a single small cooling object (for example a water jar beside the bed) to see if a hinted answer lifts interest versus the current problem-only image.
counterexample: Seq 2 shows a calmer sleeper surrounded by animals, so its tension comes from the visitors rather than the setting.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A round-headed stick figure with closed curved eyes sleeps in an orange sleeping bag with a zzz mark beside a small campfire. Three cartoon predators stand over it on a night meadow: a spotted big cat on the left, a brown bear in the middle and a spotted hyena on the right, all with wide round eyes and blue sweat drops. Stars, a crescent moon and dark mountains fill the sky.
mechanism: A safe sleeper surrounded by three nervous predators poses an inverted question: the threat is present but the animals look unwilling to act.
composition: The bear sits dead centre as the largest figure and the sleeper lies low in front of it, forming a pyramid. The cat and hyena frame both sides almost symmetrically, and the headline occupies the top band against clear dark sky.
typography: Three words in yellow capitals with a thin dark outline sit across the top and read clearly at 160x90. The words contain no animal noun, so the title's mention of animals and the count five is the only text source for the topic.
colors: A dark navy night against saturated green grass sets off the yellow headline, the orange sleeping bag and the campfire. The tan, brown and gold animal fills sit between the two backgrounds and read as separate silhouettes.
psychology: Wide eyes with visible sweat drops on all three predators show a worried look, set against the sleeper's closed eyes. The pairing of calm and unease is carried entirely by cartoon drawing.
partnership: The title says five animals are not scared of you, while the picture shows three animals that appear scared of the sleeper, so the two promises pull in different directions. The headline question gives the picture its own hook but leaves the title's list format unsupported.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the central bear's sweating face, then the sleeping figure in the orange bag, then the cat and hyena at the sides.
art: Clean flat cartoon with consistent outlines; the animal anatomy is simplified but coherent and shadows under each animal sit on the grass. Scene density is moderate and every subject stays distinct at phone size.
strength: Clear subject staging with a sleeping figure at the base of three large animals makes the setup obvious.
weakness: The animals look afraid, which sits oddly with a title about animals that are not scared.
bottleneck: Title and thumbnail tell different stories, so viewers may not know which promise to expect.
action: Hypothesis: test redrawing the animals with calm, unbothered faces to see whether the thumbnail then matches the title's not-scared claim.
counterexample: Seq 6 pairs one animal with one person and a headline that names the action, giving a tighter match to its title.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Four cartoon people stand in a suburban yard. At the left, behind a wooden fence, an older woman with a grey bun and apron waves, a bespectacled man in an apron holds a plate of food, and a bearded man with a frown points at a paper bill. At the right, a black-haired man with half-lidded eyes and a slight smile holds a mug with one hand in a pocket, and a curved red arrow runs from a yellow YOU label at top left to his head.
mechanism: The neighbours' mixed reactions (wave, food, frown and a bill) are staged against one calm figure marked YOU, so the viewer is placed in the picture.
composition: The right-hand man is the largest subject and sits at right of centre, while the three neighbours cluster in the left half beside the fence. The red arrow forms a short arc from top left to his head and the fence acts as a vertical divider between the groups.
typography: A single word in yellow capitals with a thick black outline sits at the top left and is the only text. It is small compared with the figures, so at 160x90 it is barely legible, and a faint purple rectangle outline remains visible around it. The title carries all the wealth-level framing that the picture lacks.
colors: Muted sky blue, fence brown and grey-green fill most of the frame, so the red arrow and the yellow label stand out as the only saturated accents. The lead figure's grey and black clothes keep him quiet against the pastel background.
psychology: The three neighbours show a wave, a smile with a plate, and a scowl with a pointing finger, a spread of friendly and hostile signals. The lead figure has a relaxed half-lidded look and a slight smile.
partnership: The title promises treatment across every wealth level, while the picture shows a single scene with no money cue except the bill, so it adds the neighbours' reactions but not the wealth axis. The unanswered question is which condition each reaction belongs to.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red arrow and yellow YOU first, then the black-haired man's face, then the frowning bearded neighbour with the bill, then the waving woman.
art: Soft flat cartoon with consistent line weight and coherent fence and house perspective. The visible rectangular outline around the YOU label looks like a leftover selection box, which slightly lowers polish, and the label is small at phone size.
strength: Contrasting neighbour reactions in one frame create a quick social-comparison story.
weakness: The YOU label is small and the scene gives no sign of a wealth level.
bottleneck: The only text is a tiny label, so the wealth tiers in the title are not visible in the image.
action: Hypothesis: test adding a short wealth cue such as a price tag or house tier word beside the right-hand figure to see whether the scene reads as a wealth comparison.
counterexample: Seq 8 puts big dollar figures on each panel so its wealth axis is visible at once.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: Five helmeted cartoon warriors line up in front of three burning wooden buildings under a lavender sky. A large bearded figure in a horned helmet holds a blood-streaked axe at the centre, flanked by a small round-headed figure and a bearded figure on each side and a braided figure holding a sword at the far right. Red spatter marks the clothing and a few bodies lie on the ground, with round shields at the lower left and centre.
mechanism: A frowning warrior line-up before burning buildings visualises the title's terrifying theme, and the headline supplies a brag-like verdict.
composition: The horned central figure is the largest subject and anchors a symmetrical line of five. The headline sits across the top, the fires form a ragged horizon behind the figures, and the shields cut off the bottom edge.
typography: Two words in thick yellow capitals with a dark outline run across the top and stay readable at 160x90. The headline does not repeat the title's words and adds a judgment of the warriors that the title only implies.
colors: Lavender sky and brown ground are the calm base, and orange fire and red blood marks are the warm accents. The yellow headline is separated by its outline against the pale sky.
psychology: Furrowed brows, down-turned mouths and blood-streaked clothing signal aggression, and the burning village adds a danger cue. All cues are cartoon drawing.
partnership: The title asks what made Vikings so terrifying and the thumbnail answers with imagery of raiding violence plus a short verdict, so it shows part of the answer. The unanswered piece is the actual reasons.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the central horned warrior's face, then the burning buildings, then the flanking figures.
art: Flat hand-drawn cartoon with consistent outlines; the native file is a low-resolution 480x360 so edges look soft when enlarged. The crowd of five and the fire create moderate clutter but the headline survives at phone size.
strength: The central horned figure and burning backdrop give an instant raid story.
weakness: Native resolution is low and the lower half is crowded with shields, blood marks and bodies.
bottleneck: The lineup of near-identical frowning faces gives viewers no single new detail to be curious about.
action: Hypothesis: test cropping to the central warrior and two flanking figures with larger scale to see whether a simpler lineup reads more clearly than five.
counterexample: Seq 17 also stages a group of menacing figures, but it adds a laptop and cash prop that tell a specific story.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A greyscale scene shows one thick white lightning bolt running from the top to a bright glow on a dark ground, with a tiny black stick figure with splayed limbs just beside its base. About eight thinner branching bolts hang across the sky at both sides, and dark scrubby ground marks and a small cross-like post sit along the horizon. A red circle at the bottom left holds a black silhouette of a dangling dinosaur with the words what if? in white.
mechanism: A single overwhelming bolt striking a minuscule figure turns the title's all-lightning-at-once idea into a scale contrast.
composition: The central bolt forms a bright vertical axis at the middle, with the glow at its base as the focal point and the stick figure as a tiny secondary point. Branches arc symmetrically left and right, and the dark foreground and red badge at bottom left anchor the frame.
typography: The only text is the white lower-case what if? in a red circle at the bottom left, which stays legible at 160x90. The picture carries no title words, so the premise of all lightning at once comes only from the title.
colors: Near-monochrome greys and white with a single saturated red-coral badge as the only colour. The black stick figure is the sole dark mark inside the bright glow, giving strong subject separation.
psychology: The stick figure has no readable expression at this size; its splayed limbs suggest being thrown, and the blinding bolt carries the danger cue.
partnership: The title poses a hypothetical about all lightning striking one place, and the thumbnail shows a bolt striking a tiny figure there, so it illustrates the premise without adding a number or outcome. It reveals no answer.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the bright central bolt first, then the glow and tiny stick figure at its base, then the red badge at bottom left.
art: Soft grey gradients, noise texture and crisp white bolt edges give a clean graphic look; the bolt forks and glow are internally consistent. Background complexity is low and the bolt survives at phone size, though the stick figure nearly disappears.
strength: High-contrast bolt in an otherwise greyscale frame makes a strong single focal axis.
weakness: The stick figure that gives the scale joke is too small to see at 160x90.
bottleneck: Without any words in the picture, the premise depends on the title for meaning.
action: Hypothesis: test enlarging the stick figure to about twice its current size to see whether the scale contrast reads in the 160 sheet.
counterexample: Seq 9 uses the same series badge and greyscale style but shows a split ground, so it relies on a different visual cue.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A smooth blue cartoon dolphin with a dot eye and a faint smile rises from dark blue water at the left. At the right, a brown-haired cartoon man in a blue shirt is waist-deep in the water, with wide eyes and an open mouth, reaching both hands toward a brown rocky shore. Thin ripple lines circle both figures against a pale blue sky.
mechanism: The dolphin and the struggling man share one frame so the headline can ask for a motive behind the rescue.
composition: The dolphin fills the left half and the man's face at right of centre forms the second focal point, so the picture reads left to right. The diagonal of the shore leads the eye to the reaching hands, and the sky leaves clear space for the headline.
typography: Five words in thick-outlined yellow capitals span the full width at the top and stay readable at 160x90. The headline makes the rescue explicit with the verb save, which the title only implies with the word rescue and the broader phrase wild animals.
colors: Blue dominates the water, dolphin and shirt, so the tan shore and brown hair are the only warm patches. The yellow headline pops against the pale sky, and the dolphin's mid-blue is close to the water, giving it softer separation.
psychology: The man has wide eyes, an open mouth and outstretched hands, which read as alarm. The dolphin's small smile gives a calm counterpoint.
partnership: The title generalises to wild animals rescuing us, while the thumbnail narrows to one dolphin and one man, adding a specific case and the question of motive. The reveal risk is low because no reason is shown.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the man's wide-eyed face, then the dolphin's head, then the shore he is reaching toward.
art: Clean flat cartoon with consistent outlines; the dolphin silhouette is coherent and the water line crosses both subjects believably. Background is minimal and all elements survive at phone size.
strength: Two distinct subjects with a plain background make the rescue premise clear in one glance.
weakness: The dolphin's blue merges with the water, which weakens separation of the hero animal.
bottleneck: The wild-animals plurality in the title is not visible, since only one dolphin is shown.
action: Hypothesis: test lightening the dolphin's fill or adding a white outline glow to see if the animal separates more clearly from the sea.
counterexample: Seq 2 uses a darker night scene where animals separate better from the background through contrasting fur patterns.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: CLOVE WATER BEFORE BED / BY MORNING... / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4
scene: A tumbler of water full of dried clove buds stands on a marble counter at the left. At the right, a 2x2 grid of glowing organ renders on dark blue backgrounds shows a stomach (1), intestines (2), a brain (3) and a knee joint (4), each covered in red and orange blotchy lesion-like patches. Each panel has a yellow numbered circle in its top left corner.
mechanism: A bedtime-drink photo is paired with four numbered organ images so the headline's by morning promises a visible body-wide change.
composition: The glass fills the left 40 percent and the 2x2 organ grid fills the right 60 percent, under two stacked banner bars across the top. The panels are evenly sized with little separation of emphasis, so the grid reads as a dense block.
typography: Two banner lines carry the words: black capitals on a yellow bar, then white capitals with an ellipsis on a red bar, and the numerals 1 to 4 sit in yellow circles. The banners remain readable at 160x90, while the numerals are small and the title's 7 days and unrecognizable body wording do not appear.
colors: A yellow bar over a red bar gives a strong warning-style palette, and the red-orange tissue on dark blue and the amber cloves on pale marble add saturated contrast. Red is used as an alarm signal across both the bar and the organs.
psychology: No face is visible; urgency comes from the red bar, the ellipsis and the lesion-coloured organs, which signal fear. These are colour and imagery cues only.
partnership: The title promises an unrecognisable body after 7 days, while the thumbnail shows overnight timing and four unlabelled organ states. It leaves open whether the organs are the problem or the result, which adds ambiguity rather than information.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow and red banner first, then the clove glass, then the lit organ panels in order 1 to 4.
art: A real-looking glass photo is combined with 3D-style glowing organ renders, and the two halves differ in lighting and rendering style. The organ images share a coherent glow and the grid is clear, but the mix of styles looks assembled.
strength: The large banner makes the drink-and-timing claim readable even at phone size.
weakness: The four organ panels read as red blobs at 160x90 and the lesion-like imagery suggests disease rather than a drink benefit.
bottleneck: The unlabelled organ states make the claim ambiguous, so viewers cannot tell what outcome is being promised.
action: Hypothesis: test replacing the four organ panels with one clear before-and-after cue tied to a single named effect to see if the promise becomes clearer.
counterexample: Seq 11 also uses a red-yellow health palette but names the condition in its headline so the claim is more specific.
medical_notes: The overnight timing, the vague body-wide change and the lesion-like organ images imply a rapid, unsupported effect without naming any outcome.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A two-panel split divided by a thin black vertical line. At left under $900, a cartoon man with an oversized egg-shaped head, a double chin, a white T-shirt and jeans stands flat-faced with half-lidded eyes, beside a blank white outline figure walking away. At right under $1M, the same character in a tuxedo and bow tie walks on a red carpet between stanchion posts with a slight smile, while a white outline figure bows with clasped hands and hand-drawn flash starbursts surround them.
mechanism: A mirrored before-and-after of one character at two money levels shows the treatment change from being ignored to being bowed to.
composition: Two equal halves with matching layouts make a direct left-right comparison, each topped by large numerals and a centred character below. The red carpet leads diagonally up to the right-hand figure, while the white outline figures act as secondary subjects at each panel's edge.
typography: Two large black dollar figures, one per panel, fill the top third and remain legible at 160x90. They add the concrete $900 baseline that the title lacks, while $1M restates the title's amount in shorter form.
colors: Mostly white background with black type, so the red carpet and the tuxedo are the strongest accents and the skin-tone fill separates the character. The flat white of the outline figures is deliberately blank, which pushes attention to the main character.
psychology: The character shows a flat gaze at $900 and a slight smile at $1M, while the outline figure's bowed pose and clasped hands signal deference. Cues are cartoon poses only.
partnership: The title mentions only $1,000,000, and the thumbnail adds a $900 baseline plus a visual of reverence, so the contrast is shown rather than stated. The answer to how people treat you is largely given in the picture.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the two dollar numbers first, then the left character, then the tuxedo version on the red carpet, then the bowing figure.
art: Clean vector-style cartoon with consistent outlines and flat fills; the tuxedo and carpet are coherent and the doodle starbursts are lightweight. Backgrounds are plain white, so the layout holds at phone size.
strength: A mirrored split with huge dollar figures makes the contrast instantly readable.
weakness: The right panel shows the full outcome (bowing and flashbulbs), leaving little to wonder about.
bottleneck: Reveal risk is the main limit, since the image already answers how people treat you at each level.
action: Hypothesis: test blurring or removing the bowing figure in the right panel to see if a withheld reaction raises curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 3 stages a similar social-reaction idea in a single scene without numbers, making the wealth axis harder to read.
hero_object: character in tuxedo on red carpet
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A side-on cross-section shows light-grey water above a black seabed with a V-shaped trench. A white twisting column drains from the surface line down to a small red plug at the bottom of the V. A small dark fish shape floats at the left of the column and a dark elongated shape sits on the surface line at upper right. A red circle at bottom left holds a dangling dinosaur silhouette and the words what if? in white.
mechanism: A funnel of water collapsing into one tiny red outlet gives the title's drained-oceans idea a clear mechanical picture.
composition: The white funnel forms a strong central diagonal-free vertical from the top edge to the bottom point, and the V of the seabed leads the eye down to the red dot. The black lower half and left badge give heavy weight at the bottom, while the upper area is open white.
typography: The only words are a white lower-case what if? in the red circle at bottom left, readable at 160x90 as a series label. The picture has no title words, so the oceans and the action of draining come from the title and drawing only.
colors: Black, white and mid-grey dominate, and the lone red circle and tiny red plug are the only colours, linking the badge to the focal point at the bottom of the funnel. Contrast between white column and black ground is strong.
psychology: There are no people or faces here; the cues are scale and the sense of a huge volume squeezed through one small point. Nothing signals warning beyond the red dot.
partnership: The title asks what if you drained the oceans, and the thumbnail shows the water vanishing through a hole, so the picture illustrates the premise without adding a result. It does not reveal what happens next.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white funnel first, then the red plug at its base, then the red badge at bottom left, then the small fish.
art: Clean vector-style linework with thick black outlines and flat fills; the funnel has wobbling outline detail that reads as swirling water. Background is simple and the main shape stays clear at phone size.
strength: One bold white shape on a black ground makes the drain mechanism readable at a glance.
weakness: With no figure, text or colour besides red, the image offers little emotional or human anchor.
bottleneck: The two small dark creatures are too tiny to register, so the only focal cue is the funnel shape.
action: Hypothesis: test adding a small stick figure standing at the surface edge to give the scale a human anchor and see whether the premise feels more personal.
counterexample: Seq 5 shares the badge but adds a stick figure beside the bolt, giving it a human scale cue that this image lacks.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A narrow white vertical strip sits in the centre of a 16:9 frame, with grey bars on either side. At the top left of the strip a small line of black text reads in × 9 ft × 55 mph. Below it, a small line-drawn car with a black arrow labelled 55 mph in red points toward a flat slab drawn in perspective, with a short plume of wavy lines and puff between car and slab, and red labels 1ft and 9ft on the slab's edges. A black stick figure with one hand raised stands in the lower left of the strip.
mechanism: A diagram with speed and slab dimensions suggests a back-of-envelope physics calculation, but the objects are drawn small in a mostly empty frame.
composition: The content occupies only the middle third of the width. The car, arrow and slab span the full width of the strip in an upper-middle band, with the stick figure below them at the left and the lower right of the strip left empty, so there is no clear focal pull.
typography: All text is tiny: a black formula line and three red labels (55 mph, 1ft, 9ft), each only a few pixels tall at 160x90 and not readable. No headline word states the topic, and the title's microwave and snowblower words have no visual counterpart in the text.
colors: Mostly white strip with black linework and a few red accents on the labels and arrow; the surrounding grey side bars are a flat mid-grey. There is almost no colour weight, so nothing stands out at thumbnail size.
psychology: The stick figure has no facial features and its raised hand is a minor gesture; no emotion cue is available. The numbers carry a technical, calculation tone only.
partnership: The title is a playful hypothetical about a microwave as a snowblower, but no microwave or snow is identifiable in the picture, only a car-like object, a slab and speed labels. The image adds numbers while leaving the title's key object unseen.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red 55 mph and arrow first, then the car and slab drawing, then the stick figure at lower left; the formula line is likely skipped.
art: Hand-drawn line art with thin strokes on white; the slab and car are drawn in perspective with believable proportions. The pillarbox bars waste most of the width and the artwork is far too small to survive on a phone.
strength: The red labelled arrow gives one clear speed cue inside an otherwise plain drawing.
weakness: All content is confined to a narrow centre strip with text too small to read at 160x90.
bottleneck: The tiny scale of the artwork inside grey side bars leaves nothing legible at phone size.
action: Hypothesis: test cropping to the car and slab and enlarging the 55 mph label to fill the frame to see if the diagram becomes legible at 160x90.
counterexample: Seq 8 uses its whole frame with two large dollar figures, so it is legible at 160x90 where this image is not.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: 8 SIGNS YOUR FEET HAVE / NERVE DAMAGE / FROM DIABETES / SIGN #3 IS THE DANGEROUS ONE
scene: A large close-up of a sole of a foot with creased dark skin and a reddish-orange glow across the ball and toes fills the left half, ringed by a thick red circle. Four small orange lightning-bolt marks flank the foot. At the bottom right a round inset shows a bald man with a grey beard in a white coat and teal scrubs with a stethoscope, mouth slightly open, against a dark blue background. The background is near black.
mechanism: A highlighted inflamed foot plus a numbered signs list and a teaser about one dangerous sign poses a self-check question for viewers worried about diabetes.
composition: The foot takes the left half as the dominant subject and the three text blocks stack on the right. A red bar spans the bottom under the headline, and the circular doctor inset sits at bottom right as a small third point.
typography: Four text blocks in white, yellow and white-on-red capitals rank from a small opening line to a large yellow NERVE DAMAGE, then FROM DIABETES in a red box, then a bottom red banner. The yellow phrase and the red-box line stay legible at 160x90 while the bottom banner shrinks. The count and condition repeat the title, and the sign #3 line adds a teaser.
colors: Black background with saturated yellow, red and white text and orange-red glowing skin gives very high contrast. Red is used for the circle, the bar and the banner as an alarm signal, and the orange bolts reinforce it.
psychology: The man in the inset has an open mouth and serious look, with a white coat and stethoscope as authority cues. Red circle, bolts and the word dangerous deliver fear and urgency through colour and wording.
partnership: The title asks viewers to check their feet tonight after 60, and the thumbnail repeats the signs-and-diabetes message, then adds a sign number three teaser. The unanswered question is which sign is the dangerous one, while the age cue in the title is absent.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the glowing red-circled foot first, then the yellow NERVE DAMAGE words, then FROM DIABETES in the red box, then the doctor inset and bottom banner.
art: The foot looks like an enhanced photo with artificially boosted red and orange glow, and the doctor inset is a cut-out in a circle frame. The lightning bolts are flat graphics laid over the photo, and the layout is crowded but the main words survive on mobile.
strength: Large yellow NERVE DAMAGE and a circled foot make the topic clear within a second.
weakness: Four layered text blocks plus the glowing foot make the frame dense and the bottom banner small.
bottleneck: The inset doctor carries no name or credential text, so authority rests on clothing alone.
action: Hypothesis: test removing the lightning marks and the bottom banner to see whether a simpler foot, headline and doctor layout improves clarity.
counterexample: Seq 12 gives one headline and one portrait on a calm teal field, so it avoids the layered alarm styling used here.
medical_notes: The packaging invites self-diagnosis from foot signs, uses a dangerous-sign teaser and shows a white-coat figure with no stated credential.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A woman with dark curly shoulder-length hair, drop earrings and a beaded necklace smiles with a closed mouth and looks at the viewer. She wears a white coat over a burgundy collared shirt with a navy stethoscope around her neck, shown in a rounded-corner photo panel at the right. The panel sits on a flat teal background with large words at the left.
mechanism: A stock-style portrait of a smiling clinician beside a count-and-topic headline signals a plain, trustworthy list video.
composition: The text stack occupies the left 55 percent and the portrait panel fills the right 40 percent, a clean two-block split. The face is the largest single element and sits near the right-hand third with the headline roughly centred on the left.
typography: Five words over three lines: black TOP 4 and BLOOD TESTS, then white IN AGING, all in heavy sans capitals that remain fully readable at 160x90. The line restates the title's count and topic and omits the title's kidney, liver and CBC specifics.
colors: A flat mint-teal field carries black and white type with high contrast, and the burgundy shirt is the sole warm accent. The portrait panel is separated by its rounded white-edged frame.
psychology: A closed-mouth smile, level gaze and a white coat with stethoscope present a calm professional image. No fear or urgency cue is used.
partnership: The thumbnail restates the number and topic in shorter form, adding only the portrait; the title's named organs and the older-adult framing are only partly present. Little curiosity gap is created beyond the list itself.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large black TOP 4 first, then the portrait's face on the right, then BLOOD TESTS, then IN AGING.
art: A natural portrait photo with soft background blur and even lighting is placed in a rounded panel over a flat colour block, in an editorial layout typical of slide templates. There is no visible compositing artefact and the layout survives on mobile.
strength: Large three-line headline and a clear face make the topic and a credible presenter obvious at phone size.
weakness: The flat teal layout and the generic portrait add no distinctive or curiosity-driving element.
bottleneck: Nothing in the frame creates a gap, since the headline simply restates the title list.
action: Hypothesis: test replacing IN AGING with one named test such as CBC in a contrasting colour to see whether specificity adds interest to the list.
counterexample: Seq 16 packs many cues around a similar clinician figure, which reads as noisy where this layout reads as plain.
hero_object: portrait of clinician in white coat
medical_notes: The packaging names a topic and a count only, with no cure, diagnosis or outcome claim.

scene: A blue box-shaped store with a yellow IKEA wordmark and a yellow entrance canopy stands in a grey parking lot under a cloudy blue sky. Two photographic human hands at the top edge hold wooden marionette control bars, with strings fanning down mostly to the roof, while several strings run past the building to the ground at the left, right and front. A crowd of tiny people walks toward the entrance along a yellow strip, and six cars sit in marked bays at the sides.
mechanism: The marionette strings turn a retail store into a puppet and the shoppers into small figures, implying hidden control over customers.
composition: The store is the central mass with the hands and control bars forming a symmetrical frame at top, while the strings fan down to the roof in leading lines. The crowd and yellow strip lead the eye to the entrance at lower centre.
typography: The only text is the building's own yellow wordmark, which is large and readable at 160x90; there is no overlaid headline. The title's words about customer experience and mastery have no counterpart in the picture.
colors: IKEA blue and yellow dominate against grey asphalt and a pale sky, with the yellow canopy and walkway forming a strong accent trail. The small red and blue cars add minor colour dots.
psychology: There are no readable faces; the tiny crowd and the hands above create an authority-and-control cue. The tone is slightly ominous through the puppet metaphor rather than through emotion.
partnership: The title is neutral and positive, saying how IKEA mastered customer experience, while the puppet image implies manipulation, which escalates the claim with a sinister angle. The unanswered question is how the strings work.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the IKEA sign and building first, then the hands and strings at the top, then the crowd at the entrance.
art: A photoreal render with a miniature-diorama feel; shadows and sky lighting are consistent across hands, strings and building. Most strings end on the roof, but several run past it to the ground, so the puppet logic is slightly loose; the scene still reads clearly on mobile.
strength: The puppet-string metaphor communicates control in one image without any extra words.
weakness: The image has no headline words, so it relies on the brand sign and the title for context.
bottleneck: The tiny people are too small to read emotion, so the human stakes of the metaphor stay abstract.
action: Hypothesis: test enlarging a few shoppers in the foreground with visible faces to see if the metaphor gains a human reaction.
counterexample: Seq 3 puts people with readable faces in the frame, so the social reactions are legible where this crowd is not.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

Below, a reddish-brown circle labelled Cu points through an arrow with four small additive labels to a mint circle labelled with a chemical formula, and two Statue of Liberty drawings, brown on the left and mint on the right, stand under them with COPPER and two arrowheads between them.
mechanism: A chemical-transformation diagram pairs a brown statue and a green statue, so the picture itself explains the colour change.
composition: All content is stacked in a narrow vertical strip, with the question at the top, the two circles in the middle and two matching statues at the bottom. The mirrored left-right pairing gives symmetry but each element is small.
typography: The question and chemical labels are tiny dark handwritten text on white and are unreadable at 160x90. The visible question is about the Statue of Liberty, a different subject than the title's sky colour wording.
colors: Muted brown and mint fills on white are the only colour, set against blurred green-grey bars. The brown-to-mint pairing carries the transformation meaning but with low contrast and low saturation.
psychology: The stick figure has no features and is mostly cropped by the edge. The tone is academic and calm; nothing signals urgency or fear.
partnership: The title asks why the sky is blue, while the image text asks why the Statue of Liberty is green, so the two address different questions and one is unrelated to the other. The mismatch means the picture cannot support the title's promise.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the mint and brown statue pair first, then the two coloured circles with the arrow, then the question text if it is read at all.
art: Hand-drawn line art with grainy colour fills and legible statue drawings, but the whole composition is a vertical strip centred in a 16:9 frame with blurred green-grey bars. Fine text and formulas are not legible at phone scale.
strength: The brown and mint statue pair shows a before-and-after colour change in one visual.
weakness: Text and formulas are tiny, and the topic differs from the title.
bottleneck: The question text is too small to read at 160x90, so the mismatch with the title cannot be resolved at a glance.

scene: A cartoon close-up of a man with slicked-back thinning dark hair, deep forehead lines, bloodshot red-rimmed eyes with dark bags, and an open mouth showing clenched teeth. He wears a bright red jacket over a white buttoned shirt, which fills the lower half of the frame. A hand-drawn black curved arrow at the upper right points to his head, with a handwritten two-line caption at the right.
mechanism: An exhausted-looking face paired with a bleak caption turns the title's rank-based life into a doomed-character shorthand.
composition: The face takes the left half with the head near the top and the red jacket as a wide base. The caption stacks on the right in two lines, and the arrow arcs from the caption's top to the head, linking text and subject across a blank white background.
typography: Three words in a thin handwritten style, with Dead in red and Man Walking in black, are readable at 160x90 but have a lighter stroke than a bold headline. The phrase adds a fate verdict that the title does not contain.
colors: White background with a single saturated red jacket and the red word Dead creates a strong colour echo between the figure and the caption. The black arrow and caption stay clean against white, and the skin tone separates from the red.
psychology: Wide bloodshot eyes with heavy bags, furrowed brow and a gaping clenched-teeth mouth read as distress, while the red jacket and the word dead carry a death and danger cue.
partnership: The title says your life as every rank in the Italian mafia, and the thumbnail shows a single doomed-looking figure with no mafia cue beyond the title, so it adds a bleak outcome for one rank. The unanswered question is which rank this is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the distressed face first, then the red word Dead, then Man Walking, with the arrow tying text to the face.
art: Clean vector cartoon with fine shading under the eyes and on the hair, consistent line weight, and an odd red-pink blush around the eyes that is stylised rather than an error. The plain white background keeps it very clear on mobile.
strength: The big distressed face and red-on-white palette make a fast, emotionally clear read.
weakness: Nothing visual points to the mafia or to a rank, so the title context is missing from the image.

Along the bottom are four round icons with labels: a red heart-pulse, a green leaf, a blue walking figure and a purple shield with a check. A small name badge on her scrubs reads DR. TAVINGHI PHARMACIST.
mechanism: Stacked health claims, an anatomical heart, a pointing clinician figure and a normal-looking reading try to say that one exercise safely lowers blood pressure.
composition: Text blocks fill the left 60 percent from top to bottom, the woman fills the right edge, and the heart and monitor are placed between them. Many elements compete at similar weight, with a yellow glow behind the woman and a four-icon strip across the bottom.
typography: Eight text lines in white, yellow and red-box capitals include a blue top banner, three large headline lines and four tiny icon captions. The headline lines are readable at 160x90 but the icon captions and the badge are not. The text promises one top exercise while the title promises three.
colors: A black background carries yellow, white and red text on blue and red boxes, with a golden glow behind the woman and a red heart. The result is a very high-saturation palette with red used as an alert colour for HIGH B.P.
psychology: The woman has a slight smile and a pointing hand, a friendly authority cue, while SENIORS MUST DO THIS and the red HIGH B.P box add urgency. The name badge reads a pharmacist title that the channel name does not mention.
partnership: The title says over 60, top 3 exercises and lowering blood pressure naturally, while the thumbnail says top exercise in the singular, so the count differs. Claims such as natural and safe and improves heart health add promises the title does not make.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow TOP EXERCISE headline first, then the red HIGH B.P box, then the red heart and woman's pointing hand, then the monitor.
art: A composite of a studio-lit woman cut out over a glowing background, a rendered heart and a product-style monitor, with the heart and monitor having different lighting from the woman. The layout is crowded and the bottom icon row shrinks to unreadable detail on mobile.

weakness: Eight text lines, a heart, a monitor and an icon row crowd the frame, and the icon captions are unreadable at phone size.
bottleneck: Too many competing blocks at equal weight leave the viewer without a single focal point.
action: Hypothesis: test deleting the four-icon strip and the top banner so the headline, the heart and the presenter carry the frame.
counterexample: Seq 12 uses one headline and one portrait on flat colour, giving a far clearer hierarchy than this crowded layout.
medical_notes: The badge names a pharmacist different from the channel and title name, the safe-and-natural claims are unsupported on the image, and the thumbnail says one exercise where the title says three.

scene: Three men stand behind a wooden table in front of a pale wall, seen from a first-person view with two hands in dark sleeves resting on a closed dark laptop in the foreground, a digital watch on the left wrist. At the centre a large bald man with star-shaped neck tattoos, a gold chain and rings on his fingers rests both hands flat on the table. At the left a man in a black leather jacket with sunglasses pushed up on his head holds a handgun at chest level, and at the right a man in a black tracksuit with white sleeve stripes crosses his arms. On the table sit a crushed can, four USB sticks, a phone, stacks of banded cash and a knife.
mechanism: A first-person view puts the viewer at a laptop across from armed, stern men, which turns the title's coerced-hack scenario into a literal seat at the table.
composition: The bald central figure sits at the middle and the laptop below him forms a vertical axis, with the two flanking men as near-symmetrical supports. The viewer's hands at the bottom reach upward into the frame, and the table edge splits the picture into a lower prop zone and an upper character zone.
typography: There is no overlaid text; the story rests entirely on the picture and the title. The laptop's teal glow acts as the only label-like focal cue.
colors: Black leather and dark clothing dominate against a pale wall and brown wooden table, so the teal glow under the laptop and the green cash stacks give the only cool and green accents. Skin tones and gold chains add small warm highlights.
psychology: Furrowed brows and flat stares on all three men, plus a gun, a knife and cash, supply a threat cue. The viewer's hands being placed on the laptop adds a sense of being pushed to act.
partnership: The title says the Russian mafia hired you to hack the government, and the picture supplies a threatening group, a laptop to use and cash as payment, but states neither Russia nor government in the image. It adds a concrete scene and holds back the outcome.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the bald central man's face first, then the glowing laptop, then the gun at left, then the cash and knife on the table.
art: Comic-style cartoon with consistent outlines and detailed shading on the leather jackets; the first-person hands and wrist watch share the same line style. The detail is dense but the three figures and laptop remain distinct on mobile.
strength: First-person framing at a laptop with armed men behind makes the title's scenario visible at a glance.
weakness: The table props are small and dense and the knife and USB sticks add noise at phone size.
bottleneck: With no text and no Russian or government cue, the picture can read as any crime scene.
action: Hypothesis: test adding a flag-coloured detail or a government seal on the laptop screen so the Russian and government parts of the title appear in the image.
counterexample: Seq 4 also shows a menacing group but from a flat front-on line-up, so it lacks the participatory viewpoint used here.

text: YOUR LIFE / EVERY CIA FIELD OPS RANK

mechanism: A geared-up operator drawn as a blank white mascot shows the title's rank-by-rank POV through a single military archetype.
composition: The armed figure takes the left 45 percent from top to bottom, and the text stack is placed to the right at mid-height with white space around it. The rifle points toward the lower right, creating a mild diagonal toward the text.
typography: YOUR LIFE in large white capitals on a red box is the dominant text and is readable at 160x90. EVERY CIA FIELD OPS RANK in smaller black capitals below it is thin at phone size, and the pair repeats the title wording with the POV word dropped.
colors: A white background lets the olive green helmet and dark grey gear stand out, and the red box is the single saturated accent drawing the eye to the headline. Black type under it matches the gear colours.
psychology: The scowling brows and straight mouth with a weapon and combat gear read as serious and military. No fear or hope cue is added beyond the gear.
partnership: The thumbnail text nearly restates the title's your-life and every-rank phrasing, with the figure supplying the single CIA field role. It does not show the ranks, so the every-rank promise is left to the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red YOUR LIFE box first, then the helmeted face, then the second text line, then the rifle.
art: Detailed cartoon gear with shading on the vest and helmet beside a smooth, blank round face, which gives a deliberate mascot style. The gear drawing is coherent and the white background keeps the figure and text clear.
strength: The red box makes the headline easy to read and the armed figure gives an instant role cue.
weakness: The second text line is small and thin against the heavy headline box.

scene: A cartoon man with an oversized egg-shaped head, orange-brown hair and a flat grey T-shirt rests his chin on his hand and looks sideways at the headline. mechanism: A thinking pose and a bank-with-cash picture frame the headline as a risk worry about money held in the bank.
composition: The man fills the left third, the two-line headline sits at the top right, and the bank and cash sit at lower right, forming a descending diagonal from text to money. The white background keeps three elements well separated.
typography: Three black capitals words stacked in two heavy lines, with the larger RISK... below, fill the upper right and are readable at 160x90. The word BANK on the building is tiny. The headline adds the risk judgment that the title's phrase this amount leaves open.
colors: Black type on white with green cash and a grey shirt as the main colours; the green stack is the strongest accent. There is no red, so the risk idea comes from the wording alone.
psychology: A hand-on-chin pose and sideways glance read as doubt or thought. The ellipsis after RISK adds an unfinished, hanging tone.
partnership: The title says never keep over this amount in your bank, and the thumbnail adds the reason, too much risk, along with the bank and cash picture. The unanswered question is the amount itself, which the title also hides.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large black RISK headline first, then the man's thinking face, then the arrow to the cash stack, then the bank.
art: Flat vector cartoon with clean outlines; the native file is 480x360 so edges look soft. The bank building is drawn in simple frontal view and everything stays readable at phone size.
strength: A big two-line headline with a short arrow-led path to the money keeps the message very fast to read.
weakness: The BANK label is tiny and the character is a generic thinker pose.
bottleneck: Low native resolution softens the line art when the image is enlarged.
action: Hypothesis: test replacing the ellipsis with a number placeholder such as $ ??? on the cash stack to see if the hidden amount becomes more visible.

art: Flat vector cartoon with consistent outlines and a clean white background; the cash stacks are drawn with simple banded shading. The layout holds up clearly on mobile.

weakness: The scene has no age, number or benchmark, so viewers cannot see what behind is measured against.

psychology: Wide eyes, beaded sweat, an open mouth and a pointing hand read as alarm. The red X and circled numbers add an error signal.
partnership: The title is a neutral buying-versus-leasing question, while the thumbnail asserts a mistake and shows high interest and a large price, which escalates the claim. It does not say whether buying or leasing is the wrong choice.

strength: WRONG at very large size with a visibly alarmed face lands the mistake message immediately.
weakness: The contract figures are too small to read at 160x90 and the X does not say which option is wrong.

text: NONE [CHANEL on shopping bag; licence plate CA 7XJ24]

mechanism: A modest-looking man doing yard chores is paired with a luxury car and brand-name bag, so the picture stages the idea of wealth that goes unnoticed.
composition: The man occupies the left third and the SUV fills the right two thirds, so two large subjects compete. The garage wall edge and hose coil form a vertical frame on the left, and the car's front points toward the viewer on a diagonal.
typography: No headline text is overlaid; only the CHANEL and licence plate text are visible and both are tiny at 160x90. The title's POV, rich and noticing words have no on-image counterpart.
colors: Warm orange brick and golden light dominate, so the white SUV and the green hose are the main contrast points. The navy cap and shirt are the only cool tones on the left.

art: Warm-toned flat cartoon with a more detailed, realistic rendering of the SUV and its logo than the simple character, so two rendering styles sit in one scene. The scene is rich in detail and small elements such as the bag and woman are lost at phone size.

weakness: Two large subjects of similar weight split attention and the brand and plate details are too small to read.

weakness: The wolf pack is low contrast and small at 160x90, so the ancestry idea can be missed.
